subject.title: feat(ui): custom session icons with agent-drawable SVG and nav-parity pinned rows

question: Should persisted session icons accept agent-authored SVG rendered through `unsafeHTML`, or should the supported contract be limited to curated names and single emoji?
rationale: This is a durable agent-writeable protocol and stored-state API with a new markup-sanitization boundary; implementation tests cannot choose the product’s acceptable security envelope.

options.title: Limit icons to names and emoji
options.body: Remove the `svg:` format and keep the picker plus agent support restricted to the curated registry and one emoji grapheme.

options.title: Accept the SVG security boundary
options.body: Keep `svg:` only after the responsible owners explicitly approve the supported SVG subset, threat model, and ongoing audit responsibility.

recommendation.title: Limit icons to names and emoji
recommendation.body: Remove the `svg:` format and keep the picker plus agent support restricted to the curated registry and one emoji grapheme.

likelyOwner.reason: The current head establishes the cross-surface contract and is the clearest available routing signal, though current-main ownership history remains unconfirmed.
